newsitem.title: POLAND: Centertel only bidder for Polish DCS mobile system.
newsitem.headline: Centertel only bidder for Polish DCS mobile system.

text.p: Poland's analogue mobile phone operator PTK Centertel was the only of seven prospective bidders to submit a final application for a licence to operate a digital DCS mobile network, a tender committee official said on Monday.
"Only Centertel submitted its offer," the committee's secretary said.
Among the investors which bought DCS tender documents were also France's Alcatel, Swedish Ericsson, Telecom Finland, and Poland's TPSA.

Last week the head of the committee Marian Dabrowski said the licence the the DCS system, issued together with a permit to cover the territory of at least 10 Polish provinces, would be granted by the Telecommunications Ministry by mid-September.
Centertel, in which state-owned telecoms monopolist TPSA and France Telecom have 66-percent and 34-percent stakes respectively, launched operations in Poland in 1991.
The DCS system is a more advanced version of the popular Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) cellular telephone system, using a higher frequency of 1800 MHz instead of GSM's 900 MHz.
Centertel remains a market leader with more than 185,000 customers but its competitors Era GSM and GSM Plus, which operate GSM networks are expanding quickly.
